solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Difficult restraining rook where animals feed (6)

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold something in, so TOUGH holds R inside it

blocks.note: R is the chess notation for rook

annotation.surface: A hard task: keeping a crow in check at the farmyard feeding spot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rook' reads as the bird, fitting the farmyard scene, but it is the chess piece, whose notation is R.
annotation.definitionFit: A trough is the long open container from which livestock eat or drink.

entries.clue: Chest x-ray under new rota around hospital (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, X sits under the rest
a new rota is the same letters made fresh, rearranged
the rearranged letters go around H

blocks.note: H = hospital, as on road signs
X is X-ray in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A chest X-ray is scheduled on a new hospital rota.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chest x-ray' reads as one medical phrase, but the definition stops at 'Chest' and 'x-ray' is just the letter X.
annotation.definitionFit: The thorax is the chest, the part of the body between neck and abdomen.

entries.clue: Fling a certain piece of bedroom furniture (3-5,5)

blocks.note: a nightstand is a bedside table

annotation.surface: Throwing a particular item of bedroom furniture across the room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fling' looks like a verb, to throw, but it is the noun: a brief affair. The bedroom furniture suits the answer nicely.
annotation.definitionFit: A one-night stand is a single casual sexual encounter, a fling.

entries.clue: Greek holiday, after temperature’s dropped, for Hairy Biker? (7)

indicators.note: the T for temperature is dropped from EASTER

blocks.note: GR is an abbreviation for Greek

annotation.surface: Seems to ask what Greek Easter becomes, once the heat goes, for one of TV's Hairy Bikers.
annotation.walkthrough: The Hairy Bikers were a British TV cookery duo; the question mark signals that a hairy biker is only an example of a greaser, a long-haired motorcycle rocker.
annotation.definitionFit: A greaser is a rough, greasy-haired motorcyclist, so a hairy biker is one example.

entries.clue: Councillor wears deputy’s clothing in theatre (6)

indicators.note: the deputy's letters are worn around CR, like clothes around a body

blocks.note: CR is the abbreviation for councillor
a sub is a deputy; deputy's = SUB'S

annotation.surface: A councillor dresses up in the deputy's outfit for a stage show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a stage, but it is an operating theatre, where surgeons wear scrubs.
annotation.definitionFit: Scrubs are the plain loose garments worn by surgical staff in an operating theatre.

entries.clue: Social class of actors in play mentioned (5)

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so it is how the word sounds

blocks.note: the cast is the actors in a play

annotation.surface: A play whose actors all belong to one social class.
annotation.walkthrough: CAST and CASTE are pronounced the same.
annotation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, as in the traditional Hindu system.

entries.clue: Legendary adventurer with small allowance for president once (7,1,5)

blocks.note: Ulysses is the Latin name of Odysseus, hero of Homer's Odyssey
S = small, as on clothing labels
a grant is an allowance of money

annotation.surface: A mythical wanderer receives a meagre allowance from a former head of state.
annotation.walkthrough: Ulysses S. Grant was the Union general who became the 18th US president.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Grant held the office from 1869 to 1877, and 'once' marks him as a past holder.

entries.clue: Quiet artist drinking one unknown wine (6)

indicators.note: what is drunk goes inside the drinker

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Z is an algebraic unknown, like X and Y

annotation.surface: A reserved painter sips a glass of some mysterious wine.
annotation.walkthrough: The one being drunk is swallowed by the whole of 'Quiet artist', so it lands where the two meet rather than inside the artist alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the grape, also called syrah, gives its name to a red wine.

entries.clue: Drunk person eating last of nice starters? (7)

indicators.note: a drunk person is scrambled, so PERSON's letters are rearranged
the letters take E inside them
take only the final letter of 'nice'

annotation.surface: A tipsy diner tucks into some pleasant appetisers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drunk person' reads as a sot or lush, but 'Drunk' is the anagram signal. The question mark marks openers as only one kind of starter.
annotation.definitionFit: Openers are things that start something off, such as an opening batsman or an opening remark.

entries.clue: Horse race might be won by this little man on flier perhaps (5,4)

definitions.text: Horse race might be won by this

blocks.note: a flier is a leaflet, an advertisement

annotation.surface: A small jockey riding an aeroplane, or a bird, might win the race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests something that flies, but here it is a printed flyer, an advertisement; 'perhaps' says it is one example of an AD.
annotation.definitionFit: A short head is one of the smallest winning margins in horse racing.

entries.clue: Pens used in fusty library (5)

indicators.note: the answer is found in the words that follow

annotation.surface: Writing implements in use in a musty old library.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pens used' looks like a description of old pens, but 'used in' just points into the next two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Styli, the plural of stylus, are pointed writing instruments, pens of a kind.

entries.clue: French friend emptied skips wrongly (5)

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

annotation.surface: A French pal wrongly clears out the rubbish skips.
annotation.walkthrough: A skip is a large rubbish container, so 'emptied skips' reads as a real chore.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in adverb use: 'take it amiss' means take it the wrong way.

entries.clue: “Oceanic expanse unconfined” writes European in middle of boat (4,3)

indicators.note: something 'in' a boat is aboard it, enclosed by it, so PENS and E sit within OA
take only the central letters of 'boat'

annotation.surface: A European writes a phrase about the open ocean while sitting midships.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole quoted phrase, dressed up as a heading the European is writing.
annotation.definitionFit: The open sea is the wide expanse of ocean away from land, not enclosed by coast.

entries.clue: Repeatedly unoccupied, Helena read newspaper and novel (4,5)

indicators.note: both of the next two words are emptied, keeping only their outer letters

annotation.surface: Helena, often idle, reads a paper and a novel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' makes one indicator serve two words. Hard Times is a novel by Charles Dickens.
annotation.definitionFit: Hard Times is Dickens's 1854 novel set in the industrial town of Coketown.

entries.clue: Harm English over site of battle (7)

blocks.note: O = over, the cricket scoring abbreviation

annotation.surface: An English defeat that damaged a battlefield site.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like a positional instruction, but it is simply O, an over in cricket's scorebook.
annotation.definitionFit: Marengo, in northern Italy, is where Napoleon defeated the Austrians in 1800.

entries.clue: Parisian who half chewed flan (6)

indicators.note: only the first half of CHEWED is used

annotation.surface: A Parisian who has eaten half of the flan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parisian' asks for the French word, as crossword setters use a city to signal a language.
annotation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury flan: pastry with a filling of egg and cream.

entries.clue: Idiot wearing jacket (6)

blocks.note: to be in something is to be wearing it

annotation.surface: A fool dressed in a jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' reads as a container signal, but here it is simply IN, as in 'in a suit'.
annotation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a sleeveless jacket, historically of leather.

entries.clue: Steal the show from leading male artiste at last (7)

indicators.note: take the final letter of 'artiste'

blocks.note: a team that is leading is up
a stag is a male deer

annotation.surface: Outshining the star of the show, the lead actor, at the finale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading male artiste' reads as one phrase, the leading man, but it splits into three pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: To upstage someone is to steal attention from them, originally by standing upstage of them.

entries.clue: Tree more bare, lacking breadth (5)

indicators.note: the word is without the B

blocks.note: balder = more bare, having less hair
B = breadth, as in measurements; removed

annotation.surface: A tree grows barer and thinner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lacking breadth' reads as narrow, completing the thin tree, but it asks for B to be removed.
annotation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family, common by rivers.

entries.clue: Miscreant runs fashion magazine when leader absent (5)

indicators.note: the first letter of the magazine is removed

annotation.surface: A wrongdoer takes over a fashion magazine while its editor is away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests an editor, but it just means the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or mischievous person, a miscreant.

entries.clue: Leafy vegetable cleaning lady prepared at rear (5)

indicators.note: take the final letter of 'prepared'

blocks.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British cleaning lady

annotation.surface: The cleaner has made a leafy vegetable dish in the back.
annotation.walkthrough: A char is dated British slang for a woman paid to clean a house.
annotation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green vegetable related to beet.

entries.clue: Country retreat with distinctive character (7)

blocks.note: a den is a private retreat
a mark is a distinctive sign or character; 'with' joins the pieces

annotation.surface: A rural hideaway that has real character.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country retreat' reads as a cottage in the countryside; 'Country' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one Scandinavian nation stands for the general word.

entries.clue: Tolerate quarrel periodically after goal (6)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals
these letters come after END

blocks.note: an end is a goal or aim

annotation.surface: Putting up with the occasional row after a goal is scored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goal' suggests football, but here it is an aim: an end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to put up with something unpleasant.

entries.clue: Material with great weight on bed (6)

indicators.note: TON comes on, that is after, COT

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
a ton is a great weight

annotation.surface: Bedding fabric crushed under something very heavy.
annotation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' means placed after, so the weight follows the bed.
annotation.definitionFit: Cotton is a fabric woven from the fibres of the cotton plant.
